QUICK START — try Kanau in 3 minutes

You do not need a single light to get this far. Button names are shown exactly as they appear on screen.

The app opens with a practice rig of 24 fixtures already patched. Three minutes here will show you most of how Kanau works.

1. Change the intensity

  1. Drag a fader up and down. The number above it and the color of the round icon change with it.
  2. Tap GM 100 at the top of the screen, and drag the grand master down in the panel that opens. The band at the top of the screen and its edge turn red.
  3. Tap →100 to bring it back, and close the panel.

A fader moves by the distance your finger travels, not the place you touched. Where you start makes no difference to the result.

2. Change the color

  1. Press and hold the round icon above a fader.
  2. The color panel opens. Intensity sets brightness, Color Temperature sets white, RGB sets color.
  3. The ‹ › at the top move you to the next fixture.

Every fixture carries different features, so the items you see change with it.

3. Recall a Scene

  1. Open the Scenes tab at the bottom.
  2. Five Scenes are waiting: DIM, COLOR, CCT, PIXELS, FX. Tap one.
  3. Back on Home, the faders and colors have changed to that look.

AUTO UPDATE is on to begin with, so anything you change after a recall is recorded back into that Scene. Switch the top of Scenes to MANUAL UPDATE, or lock the Scene, to leave it as it is (chapter 08).

See the values going out

Even with no lights attached, Settings → DMX Monitor shows the numbers Kanau is actually sending. Move a fader and the numbers move with it.

What is in the practice rig

The demo has 24 fixtures from Generic: DIMMER, CCT, RGB, RGBW and BAR (4 pixels). They are in three groups of eight, called KEY, BACK and FLOOR.

The grand master starts at 100, six fixtures are marked for BATTERY SAVE and carry a green label, FLOOR has a fire effect running, and five Scenes are saved. None of it claims to be a real product.

Connecting real lights

Once the demo makes sense, move to your own gear.

  1. Connect: put the iPhone on the same network as your DMX node. In Settings → Output, check that Nodes Answering is 1 or more and Network Output is green (chapter 02). Gear that does not answer polling stays at 0 while receiving normally, so judge by the light itself in that case.
  2. Patch: Patch → ＋ New Patch → Add New Fixture, then set the model, DMX mode, universe and address. Match the fixture's own settings (chapter 03).
  3. Build the look: set intensity and color on Home (chapters 04 and 05).
  4. Save it: tap SAVE in Scenes to store the look (chapter 08).

The practice rig is an ordinary show. Delete it when you patch your own lights, or make a new one with Settings → Shows → New Show.

Five things worth knowing first

  1. Fixture Lock beats blackout. A locked fixture stays lit through B.O. (chapter 10).
  2. Under AUTO UPDATE a recalled Scene records what you do. Switch to MANUAL UPDATE, or lock it, to leave it alone (chapter 08).
  3. There are three kinds of lock. Fixture Lock holds the output, Scene Lock protects what a Scene has stored, Screen Lock stops stray touches (chapter 10). With Strap Lock on, the default, the screen also locks by itself when the iPhone hangs upside down. Lifting it does not unlock it; slide right, as with SCREEN LOCK.
  4. When the grand master is below 100, the band at the top of the screen turns red and its edge pulses red. If things look dim, look there first.
  5. If another console is sending to the same lights, you will see WAITING or SHARED. Both are explained in chapter 02.
WARNING

A fixture with Lock on will not go out when you press blackout, and will not go out when you pull the grand master to zero. Check that your locks are clear before a take. The count of what is still lit during a blackout is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen.

01 Reading the screen

What is on the Home screen, from the top down, and how to read it when something looks wrong.

Learn these seven first

Before the detailed tables, these are the only places you need to know.

PlaceWhat it does
GMOverall brightness, at the top of the screen
Fixtures / GroupsChooses which fixtures appear
FaderSets intensity
ScenesStores looks and brings them back
PatchRegisters fixtures
EffectsLists and stops running effects
SettingsOutput, shows, MIDI, session

Everything below is the detail.

The five tabs

Home is where you work. Tapping another tab opens a panel over it. Drag the handle at the top down, or tap Done, to come back to Home.

TabWhat it is forSee
ScenesSaving and recalling looksChapter 08
PatchFixtures, addresses, modes, groupsChapter 03
HomeSetting intensity with fadersChapter 04
EffectsListing, adjusting and stopping effectsChapter 09
SettingsDMX output, shows, MIDI, session, preferencesChapters 02, 11–13

The status line

On the left is the route and the connection state. The route is a single letter: A for Art-Net, S for sACN. The dot beside it pulses while DMX is going out. Bluetooth carries its own dot and name. Next to them is the name of the show you are in; on a narrow phone, where the row has no room to spare, it is left out. While BLIND is on, this whole left part becomes an amber BLIND; tap it to leave BLIND (chapter 08).

ShownMeaning
Green dotSending
Amber dotSlowed down, or reconnecting (Reconnecting…)
Red dot, No nodeNothing is answering
Red dot, BlockedSomething is stopping the output that will not clear by itself. This word is all the status line says; Settings → Output prints the reason, and what to do about it, in red
Grey dot, IdleStopped
WAITING and an IPAnother console was found, so this one is holding back
SHARED and an IPAnother console is sending to the same universe. This one is still sending too
JOINED and a nameIn a session. DMX goes out from the host

A green dot does not prove the light received anything. Chapter 02 explains how to check; chapter 14 covers what to do when it goes wrong.

The middle and right of the line carry these.

ItemTapHold, or note
GM 100Opens the grand master panelHold for its settings. Below 100 it is filled red and pulses
B.O.Clears the blackoutReplaces GM while the console is dark. B.O. is also shown when GM is 0
U1 OFF (red)NothingWhich universes are switched off, by number. Up to three, then + for more. Turn them back on in Settings → Output
🔒 n (green)NothingWhat is still lit while the console is dark: locked fixtures, faders set as a switch that are ON, and locks left at an old address
BATTERY SAVETurns it on and offHold to set the amount and the fade. While it is on, it now and then shows the current amount, such as −50%
SCREEN LOCKDoes not lockHold for 0.5 seconds to lock the screen

U1 OFF and 🔒 appear only when there is something to report: the first when a patched universe is switched off, 🔒 while the console is claiming dark, which is a blackout or the grand master at zero. With Strap Lock on, hanging the iPhone upside down also locks the screen; slide right to unlock it.

The parts of Home

ItemHow to use it
Fixtures / GroupsSwitches between showing by model and showing by group
10 / 5Faders on a page. Five makes each one wider
HISTORYOpens the list of earlier states
Model and group buttonsTap to show those fixtures. Hold to set color and intensity for all of them
CLEAR nClears the selection. The light does not change
‹ / ›Moves between pages
NumberIntensity from 0 to 100. Shown large at the top while you drag
Round fixture icon (…)Tap to select. Hold to open that fixture's panel
FaderDrag up and down to set intensity
Model nameMarks a run of the same model and mode
Number buttonThe fixture number. In piano mode it changes intensity while held
⏻Turns the output off and on, keeping the value
COLORSets color and intensity for the selected fixtures
EFFECTApplies an effect to the selected fixtures
PIXELSOpens and closes the cells of pixel fixtures
＋ −Cycles piano mode: LOCK → ＋ → −
FINECycles sensitivity: normal → FINE (1/10) → FINE+ (1/100)

COLOR is unavailable with nothing selected, and with fixtures that have no color. EFFECT needs a selection. PIXELS needs a pixel fixture on the page.

Colors and marks

Color or markMeaning
AmberSelected, or active
RedBlackout, a low grand master, a network problem, piano mode. Something to check
GreenSending. Fixture Lock. BATTERY SAVE on
Amber band and edgeBLIND is on. What you do does not reach the lights
PurpleOutput switched off, or the screen locked
CyanBeing worked by the other device in a session
OrangeAt a limit you set
GreyUnavailable, or stopped

The round icon carries the fixture's color and its real output. On a fixture with pixels it reads the cells as well, so one sitting at 100 with every cell down shows dark. A selection shows an amber rim, a switched-off output a purple ring and ⏻, a lock a green outer ring and 🔒. A running effect makes it move.

A red edge runs around the screen whenever the grand master is below 100, or during a blackout. The edge pulses, and a light travels around it. At zero — or in a blackout — the edge becomes thicker and deeper, and the light travels faster, so the two states are told apart without reading anything. A green edge, with a long light sliding slowly around it, means BATTERY SAVE is on. When both apply, the edge takes turns: red for about six seconds, green for about two. BLIND looks different: the band at the top of the screen, where the clock is, and the edge become one amber frame. If the grand master is down during BLIND, a red edge pulses on the amber frame. Green is not shown during BLIND. The edge says the output is being held down; the chip in the status line says by what.

02 Sending DMX — Output

Setting up the link to your lighting gear, and checking that it is getting there.

First connection

One Art-Net node

  1. Put the iPhone on the same Wi-Fi or wired network as the node.
  2. Open Settings → Output.
  3. Choose Art-Net and AUTO. Both are the defaults.
  4. Check that Nodes Answering is 1 or more and Network Output is green. Some gear never answers polling and stays at 0 while it is receiving normally, so do not stop here if the figure will not move — carry on to step 5 and let the light answer instead.
  5. Move a fader on Home and watch the light respond.

Kanau sends every patched universe continuously, normally at 44 Hz. There is no start button. Sending can pause or stop when another console is detected, when the network settings change, or when iOS withholds permission.

Settings in detail

Protocol and networks

Art-Net and sACN are exclusive: pick one. CRMX over Bluetooth runs alongside either.

Network lists your Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Hotspot connections with their addresses and how many nodes answered on each.

  • By default it uses every network available.
  • From the all-selected state, tapping one leaves only that one on. After that each tap turns one on or off.
  • With only one network, tapping it stops network output, and tapping it again goes back to using it.
  • Turn them all off and nothing goes out over the network. Bluetooth keeps sending.
  • A connection marked No address cannot be selected.

If you use wired and Wi-Fi together, check that both appear in the list.

Choosing the destination

SettingWhere it sendsWhen to use it
AUTO (Art-Net)Each universe by unicast to the nodes that list it in their reply; a node that lists none gets them all. Plus one broadcast a second on each network. Broadcast only, if nothing answeredThe normal choice
BROADCAST (Art-Net)Every frame to each network's subnetWhen a node reports a wrong address and AUTO updates slowly
UNICASTStraight to the addresses you enterWhen broadcast does not reach, or you want to name the target
255.255.255.255 (Art-Net)Broadcast on the segment. Does not cross a routerWhen addressing does not line up and ordinary broadcast fails. iOS may block it
MULTICAST (sACN)The multicast address for each universeThe sACN default

With UNICAST, type the node's address and tap Add. With none entered you get No node IPs entered. and nothing is sent. Every universe goes to every address you enter.

If Nodes Answering is 1 or more on AUTO but the lights only update about once a second, check whether the node is reporting the wrong address for itself. Look at Destination and try BROADCAST. Chapter 14 covers the other causes of lag.

RESCAN

Tapping RESCAN under Art-Net refreshes the node list. Use it after adding gear, removing gear or changing an address. Left alone, a new node appears within about 3 seconds and a removed one disappears after about 10.

Sending continues while it scans. RESCAN is unavailable with no usable network.

When the output stops

In Settings → Output, a red line says what stopped the output and what to do about it: turn on the local network permission, switch to UNICAST and type the node's address, check the address you typed, check the Wi-Fi, give the node power. CRMX carries a line of its own. The console's own wording stays in brackets at the end, so it can be quoted exactly.

Universes and Art-Net numbering

Universes lists each patched universe with its fixture count, how many are lit, and an ON/OFF switch.

IMPORTANT

OFF does not stop sending. It keeps sending zeros to that universe, so that a receiver cannot sit holding its last values and stay lit. Which universes are switched off is named at the top of the screen, as U1 OFF.

If your node wants Net / Sub-Net / Universe instead of a single number, turn on Settings → Settings → Art-Net → Net / Sub / Uni. The relationship is Net × 256 + Sub × 16 + Uni.

sACN priority can be 0, 100 or 200. The default is 100. Where several sources send the same universe, the receiver follows the highest priority.

CRMX over Bluetooth

  1. Turn on Bluetooth in Settings → Output → CRMX (Bluetooth).
  2. Allow Bluetooth the first time iOS asks.
  3. Pick a transmitter from the list. Tapping it again disconnects.

The transmitter you pick carries universe 1 (U1). Next time, turning Bluetooth on reconnects to the same one. Scanning stops once the ones you picked are connected, so RESCAN is how you look for another transmitter. The list says connected for one that is linked and sending for one that data is going to. When a transmitter cannot connect or drops out, Settings → Output says what to check, with the system's own message in brackets.

With the same universe going out over both the network and Bluetooth, Settings → Output says so: U1: network and Bluetooth output are both on. That is a statement of fact, not a warning. A CRMX receiver takes the output of the transmitter it is linked to, so the same U1 on Kanau does not by itself feed one fixture twice. Flicker only happens where a fixture really is receiving from both paths; stop one of them there.

If a transmitter refuses Art-Net after you turn Bluetooth off, check its own Bluetooth setting and restart it. On the Aputure Sidus Four, check the Sidus BT setting on the unit as well.

When another console is found

ShownWhat it means, and what to do
WAITING + IPAnother console was already sending when this one started, so this one is holding back. Stop the other one, or tap the message and choose Send anyway? → Send. If the other one is a Kanau host, you can join its session instead
SHARED + IPAnother console appeared after this one started. Sending continues, so stop one of them if you need to

If two devices start together and both hold back, the one with the lower address starts sending again.

DMX Diagnostics — reading what is happening

The lower half of Output is there to show you where things stopped. It is not a set of settings. When output is slow or missing, read it from the top (chapter 14).

ItemHow to read it
DestinationWhere it is really going. ↦ after an address means unicast to a node that answered
MediumThe connections in use, for example Wi-Fi + Ethernet
Network OutputPackets sent over the network in the last second. Around 44 is normal. Nothing means none went out. Bluetooth is not counted here
ClockThe worst gap between sends. About 23 ms is normal. Over 100 ms points at the phone
Touch → WireFrom your finger to the packet. About 25 ms is normal
Nodes AnsweringHow many answered, with name, address, connection and round trip. The figure in brackets is the worst of the last 10 seconds. On AUTO, the line under each node lists the universes sent to it, such as U1 or U0–U3
Type these into the nodeThe Net / Sub / Uni to enter on the node, when that display is on

These narrow the problem down; they do not prove success. They are what Kanau sent, and whether the light received it cannot be seen from here. Network Output can be green while a mismatch or a fault at the other end keeps the lights dark. Gear that does not answer polling shows 0 under Nodes Answering even while it is receiving.

DMX Monitor

Settings → DMX Monitor shows all 512 channels of each universe as they go out. It refreshes 10 times a second. Reading it does not affect sending.

The cells only show values; nothing can be typed here. A lock whose fixture has been deleted is listed above the grid, with UNLOCK.

The values read as percent or as raw DMX, following the same setting as the rest of the console. Each universe folds away on its own; a folded heading keeps the count of channels still showing, so you can see which one is busy without opening it.

03 Patching fixtures — Patch

Register the lights you are using, and set the model, DMX mode, universe, address, number and groups.

Intensity and color are set on Home (chapters 04 and 05).

Adding fixtures

  1. Open Patch → ＋ New Patch and tap Add New Fixture to show the fields.
  2. Choose Manufacturer → Fixture → Mode. The mode must match the one set on the fixture itself. Each of the three opens as a list of its own with a search field, so a long list of models is a matter of typing rather than scrolling.
  3. Set how many, the universe and the start address.
  4. Check the range and any warnings, then tap Add. It is saved as it is added.
FieldWhat it is
FavoritesA ★ sits beside each mode, the Mode field and each manufacturer; tap it to add or remove. Starred modes appear as buttons under Favorites, starred manufacturers go to the top of the list, and Edit beside Favorites lists them all
NameThis fixture's own name. It appears in Patch and the Patch List; Home shows the Label instead. Defaults to the model name
Number / How ManyThe number you call it on the floor, and how many to add, up to 4,096. The number may be left empty; it starts at the highest in use plus one
LabelThe display name shared by every fixture of that model. It runs under the faders. Defaults to the official model name. It can also be typed in the title of the fixture's panel (chapter 06)
Universe / AddressDefaults to U1 / 1. Changing the universe resets the address to 1. U0 is allowed
OffsetThe spacing between fixtures. Filled in from the mode's channel count
GapExtra channels to leave between fixtures
BATTERY SAVEMarks the new fixtures for BATTERY SAVE
Label ColorThe background of the number. Seven colors, or none
MapThe 512-channel layout. Drag and release to set the start address

Each fixture after the first starts at the previous start address plus Offset and Gap, but never closer than the mode's channel count, so the addresses do not overlap. Anything past 512 goes into the next universe. An Offset smaller than the mode's channel count raises a warning, but you can carry on.

Afterwards a panel lists what went in — one row per fixture, with its number, name and address — under a line like Added 3 × Titan Tube — U1 1–15. It stays until you tap OK, so you can keep patching and read it after. Already Patched lets you add more of a model you already have. Patched Now shows the current layout.

Two kinds of number

NumberWhat it is
Unit No.A running number within the model. Assigned for you
Fixture NumberThe number you use on the floor. You set it

Which one Home shows is set in Settings → Settings → Fixture Numbers → Show the Fixture Number. Unit No. is the default. Duplicate fixture numbers raise a warning but are allowed.

Models and modes

This version ships with 46 manufacturers, 680 fixtures and 13,151 modes. For anything not in the library, use the Generic definitions or Custom Fixtures.

Generic includes Dimmer, Dimmer 16-bit, Bi-color, CCT, RGB, RGBW, Dimmer + RGB, Dimmer + RGBW, Bulb and Desk lamp.

  • PROVISIONAL (Advanced): a placeholder mode, used where the DMX chart has not been worked through. It sends intensity on channel 1 and nothing else.
  • Modes with no dimmer channel: the fader drives the color channels together, acting as a virtual dimmer.

Changing patched fixtures

Patched lists fixtures by model and mode. Tap a heading to fold it. Tap a fixture's row to open its patch settings.

Patch List, under the Patched heading, shows every patched fixture in address order, universe by universe. Each row reads the universe and the start address large with the end address under it, the fixture's number, then its name and mode; modes are never cut short. It is there to read while you set addresses on the fixtures themselves; nothing in it can be changed. An overlapping start address is red and marked ⚠. Export PDF at the top right makes an A4 copy to hand out, with the show name and the date on each page.

Fixture Sheet, in Settings just below DMX Monitor, shows how every fixture is right now, in the order of All on Home: number and name, address, intensity, color, any running effect, and marks such as LOCK and OFF. Nothing in it can be changed, and Export PDF makes a copy.

Labels, in Settings below Fixture Sheet, makes stickers for the fixtures as an A4 PDF, in address order. Standard is 52.5 × 37.125 mm, 32 to a sheet; Small is 26.25 × 14.85 mm, 160 to a sheet. Copies sets 1 to 4 per fixture. Each label carries the fixture number, the Label, the start address and the mode. Export PDF saves it.

⚠ marks an overlapping address or a run past channel 512. It also marks a fixture whose output is being held at other values, by a lock; open the fixture to see it. Sending continues while it is showing, so check the settings. n fixture data problems refers to faults found while loading fixture data; tap it for the detail.

Working in this list does not change which fixtures Home is showing.

Changing many at once

Tap Select Many and choose the fixtures. The ✓ on a model row takes all of that model.

ActionWhat it does
Select All / Select NoneTakes or clears everything, folded rows included
NameNumbers the end of the name in the order you selected
NumberSets fixture numbers in the order you selected
AddressRe-lays them from a universe, start address and gap
BatteryMarks or unmarks them for BATTERY SAVE
New groupBuilds a group from the selection
DeleteRemoves them. Check the count before you confirm

Deleting a fixture also removes its intensity, color and limits, and takes it out of every Scene. HISTORY can undo it. Deleting from within a group only removes it from that group; the fixture itself stays. If that leaves the group empty, the group is deleted too, and the confirmation says so.

Re-patch — moving into free space

  1. Open Patch → Re-patch.
  2. In the address-ordered list, choose the fixture to move.
  3. Tap a free range. It moves to the start of it.

Only ranges large enough are offered. Overlapping fixtures are shown in red.

Close Gaps, at the top right of Re-patch, packs the fixtures of one universe from address 1, in address order. It lists only the fixtures that move, with Before and After, and nothing changes until you tap Apply. The fixtures' own DMX addresses do not change: set each fixture to its After value. Locked addresses keep their previous values. The whole pack is one step in HISTORY.

Building groups

  1. Tap ＋ New Group and give it a name.
  2. Choose the fixtures in the order you want them on Home.
  3. Tap CREATE.

A fixture can be in several groups. It is not copied: changing it from any group changes the same fixture. Adding it to a group leaves it in All.

Tapping a group name lets you set the name, see the count and address range and layout, reorder, or delete it. Edit Group — Add & Reorder adds and rearranges fixtures; Add to an Existing Group puts the current selection into a group you already have.

Whether Patch shows an All row is set in Settings → Settings → Groups → Show the All Row.

Fixtures not in the library (Advanced)

Custom Fixtures holds definitions you add yourself. It is on the Patch tab, under ＋ New Patch and the list of models. They are available to every show. Deleting a definition does not affect fixtures already patched from it.

From GDTF Share

  1. Open ＋ Browse GDTF Share and SIGN IN with your GDTF Share account.
  2. REFRESH the list, then choose manufacturer, fixture, revision and mode. Search covers every manufacturer.
  3. Read the import report and choose SAVE, SAVE & EDIT or SAVE & PATCH.

SAVE & PATCH opens the patch screen with that definition selected. Remember on This Device stores your sign-in; FORGET removes it. Definitions you already fetched stay. Your sign-in goes to GDTF Share.

From a GDTF file

＋ Import a GDTF File → ＋ Open a GDTF File, pick the .gdtf, check the mode and the import report, then save. No network is needed.

The report lists what could not be carried over. A 16-bit value split across distant addresses keeps only its coarse byte, unused addresses are held as empty slots, and channels on another DMX break are dropped. Where addresses overlap, the earlier channel wins. Unknown functions keep their original names.

A definition marked Imported data is not verified. should be checked against the real fixture. Fix wrong roles with SAVE & EDIT; the fix applies to fixtures you patch from it afterwards. This mode has no channels. means you should pick a different mode.

By hand, from a DMX chart

Open ＋ Build by Hand and start from an empty definition or a template: Dimmer, CCT, Bi-color, RGB, HSI, x y, CCT + HSI, Dimmer + RGBW, Full Color, Full Color + White, Multi-emitter. The second choice, Copy an Existing Fixture, starts from a fixture in the library instead (below).

Give each channel a label, and set the role, 8 or 16 bit, default and real-world unit as needed. Channel numbers and the total are worked out for you. Leave a slot unused if you do not know its role, and you can still drive it from Channels. CREATE refuses to save while there is an ERROR.

By copying an existing one

Open ＋ Build by Hand → Copy an Existing Fixture and choose Manufacturer, Fixture and Mode. The copy is named "… (Modified)" and is listed under MODIFIED in the Manufacturer list. Duplicate and Edit lets you change the name, the color temperature range, channel roles and names, labels and defaults. The channel count, the 16-bit layout, the ranges and the switch structure cannot be changed.

04 Setting intensity — Home

The faders on Home. This is the heart of Kanau.

Moving a fader

A fader responds to the distance your finger travels, not to the place you touched. You can drive it from the number, the round icon, or the empty space below the fader. It is built so you can work while looking at the stage instead of your hand.

The knob grows a little as you touch it, and nothing moves until you have dragged a short way, so resting a finger on it is safe. While you drag, the number, the name shown under the faders and the value appear large at the top of the screen. If you have set limits, it moves within them. On a fixture that carries color, the readout also shows that color as a band, the color temperature in kelvin, G or M with a number when the green / magenta tint is off neutral, and the name of the gel or preset in use. A plain dimmer shows none of that, and the grand master never shows a color, because it is not one fixture.

FINE

ActionWhat happens
Short tapCycles normal → FINE (1/10) → FINE+ (1/100) → normal
HoldThe next step while held. Back to normal when you let go

Switching mid-drag does not make the value jump. FINE also applies to raw channels and to Pan and Tilt.

Moving several at once

Select two or more round icons, then drag one of the faders. They all move by the same amount, keeping the differences between them. When one reaches a limit the others carry on. Locked fixtures are left out.

This is not the same as working several fixtures in the COLOR panel, where they all land on the same value. The exception there is the ratio row under Intensity, which scales each fixture from its own level (chapter 05).

The number buttons as a piano

The ＋ − button at the bottom right sets the mode.

ModeWhile a number button is held
LOCK (the default)Nothing changes
＋Goes to the Piano ＋ level, 100 by default. Never above the fixture's upper limit, and never lowers a fixture that is already higher
−Goes to the Piano − level, 0 by default. Never below the fixture's lower limit, and never raises a fixture that is already lower

Let go and it returns to where it was. You can hold several at once, or slide sideways to play them in turn. Locked fixtures do not respond.

The buttons turn red while ＋ or − is armed. It is always LOCK at launch. The two levels are set in Settings → Settings → Piano ＋ and Piano −, for this device; when either differs from 100 or 0, the ＋ − button shows it, as ＋80 or −20.

⏻ — output only

Tapping ⏻ turns a fixture's output off and on while keeping the value. It turns purple while off, and the number stays. Moving the fader while it is off does not light anything.

ON/OFF is the default. In the fixture's Switch Function you can change it to FLASH ON or FLASH OFF, which last only while held, or to NONE. Locked fixtures do not respond.

The fifth choice is LOCK: the square then turns that fixture's lock on and off. A square set to LOCK is the one thing a lock does not stop — if it did, a locked fixture could never be unlocked from here.

A fader as a switch

Turn on Switch in a fixture's panel (chapter 06) and its fader becomes a rocker the full length of the fader: ON at the top, OFF at the bottom. Each tap switches it the moment you press. ON goes to the upper limit and OFF to the lower limit, and the number above reads ON or OFF. Dragging, FINE and ZEN do not work on it.

GM, BATTERY SAVE and intensity effects do not lower it. B.O. turns it off, and ⏻ and Lock work as usual. A value that arrives another way, from a Scene, MIDI or the COLOR panel, lands on ON at 50 or above and on OFF below 50. In a Scene fade it switches at the start. With the piano, ＋ is ON and − is OFF while held.

GM and B.O.

Tapping GM at the top opens the grand master fader, B.O. and →100.

  • The GM fader sets overall brightness. It is relative, and FINE works on it.
  • B.O. turns the blackout on and off. The GM value is kept.
  • →100 appears when GM is below 100, and puts it back.

Holding GM offers 100, 75, 50, 25, 12.5 and 0. The 0 there turns the blackout on; it does not set GM to zero.

The fade for these buttons is set in Settings → Settings → Master Fade. SNAP is the default. Dragging the fader with a finger is always immediate.

WARNING

A fixture with Lock on does not respond to GM or B.O. It stays lit. The count of what is still lit during a blackout, locked fixtures included, is shown next to the green 🔒 at the top of the screen.

Choosing what is on the page

Fixtures shows by model and mode; Groups shows All and the groups you built. Tap a name to switch. One fader is always one fixture, even inside a group.

The order under All is set in Settings → Settings → Order on All, either by model and running number or by fixture number. Inside a group it is the order you built.

‹ and › change page. Switching between 10 and 5 keeps the fixture you are working on in view. While you hold a fader, none of these — the names, ‹ and ›, 10 and 5, PIXELS or PIANO — changes what is on the page; pressing one gives a warning vibration instead.

The buttons along the bottom

COLOR needs a selection. EFFECT takes one too, but it also opens with nothing selected while something is running anywhere on the rig; it goes grey only when nothing is selected and nothing is running. PIXELS goes grey when there is no pixel fixture on the page.

Working pixels on their own

Tapping PIXELS opens the cells of any pixel fixtures on the page as their own faders. They follow the fixture's own fader with the keys .1, .2 and so on, and each carries its own intensity and color. Tap again to fold them.

A fixture with pixels carries P above its value. A fixture whose pixel order is inverted (chapter 06) carries R instead, and its pixel faders run the other way: the leftmost is the last pixel.

Select more than one cell and they move together on one fader, the same way fixtures do: each keeps its distance from the others, and the ones that reach an end stop there.

CLEAR n only clears the selection. Values and outputs are untouched.

05 Setting color — COLOR

Color and intensity for one fixture or many.

NOTE

What you see depends on what the fixture actually has. A one-channel dimmer shows only Intensity. Kanau does not show controls a fixture does not have.

Opening the panel

HowWhat it works on
Hold a fixture iconThat one fixture
Hold a cell iconThat cell
Select fixtures, then COLOREverything selected
Hold a model or group buttonEvery fixture in it. All means every fixture

With one fixture open, ‹ and › move to the next.

Intensity and color

ItemHow it works
Intensity0 to 100, by slider, typing, ± buttons, presets or the ratio keys
Color Temperature (CCT)In kelvin, within the fixture's range
Green / MagentaThe green–magenta correction. Back to neutral returns it to 0
CrossfadeThe balance between the white side and the color side. Which way round is up to the fixture
RGB and emittersR, G, B, W, Amber, Lime, Cyan and whatever else the fixture carries
Hue / Saturation / CIE x / CIE yShown on fixtures that have them

Intensity ±5 and ±10 snap to multiples of 5 or 10: from 47, +10 gives 50. The presets are 0, 10, 20, 30, 50, 75 and 100. Under them, 1/8, 1/4 and 1/2 set the level to that part of what it is now, and ×2, ×4 and ×8 multiply it, up to 100.

The CCT presets are 2700, 3000, 3200, 4300, 5000, 5600, 6500 and 10000 K. Beyond the fixture's range you land on its limit, marked MIN or MAX. A fixture with only two color temperatures shows two buttons instead of a slider.

The Green / Magenta steps can be edited by holding them. Where a fixture has more than one crossfade, the later ones appear just above the controls they feed.

Gels

ItemWhat it is
Gel presetsLEE and Rosco presets for fixtures with RGB. Separate tables for 3200 K and 5600 K
Preset / GelThe fixture's own built-in gels or color presets, chosen by number
Gels → x/yLEE and Rosco chromaticities for fixtures with x and y

The RGB values under Gel presets come from Astera's published color data. They carry no brightness, so set that with the fader. With a fixture's built-in presets, the app cannot always show which one is selected.

The list stays open after you pick, so you can try one after another. Close it with ✕. Whether it appears at all is set in Settings → Settings → Gels → Gel presets.

Saving colors you use often

  • Save this color stores a color under ★. It is kept per model. CCT and G/M are not included.
  • Save this temperature stores a color temperature. That one is shared across models.

Tap a stored button to apply it. Hold to rename, edit or delete.

Advanced Color

Advanced Color gathers the controls the app works out for itself, rather than the fixture's own channels.

In the picker, hue runs across and saturation down. Brightness is the fader's job. Drag near the round handle to move the color; anywhere else scrolls the panel.

RGB, the Hue and Saturation worked out from RGB, and CMY (255 − RGB) appear on fixtures that can take them. On a fixture that receives only Hue and Saturation, or only x and y, use the controls higher up instead.

Several fixtures, and several models

In this panel, whatever you touch lands on the same value for everything selected. That is true of the sliders, the ± buttons, the presets, typing and the stored colors alike. To move them while keeping their differences, select the faders on Home instead. The one exception is the ratio row under Intensity: 1/8 to ×8 scale each fixture from its own level, so their differences stay.

With different models selected, only Intensity, CCT, G/M, Crossfade and ★ appear. Open one model on its own to set RGB and emitters. CCT is held within each fixture's own range.

Pixels and repeated color groups

Hold a cell icon to set that cell's color and intensity. Changing the body color sets every cell; a cell you changed by hand keeps its own. The body Intensity applies across all the cells.

Where a mode carries the same color role more than once, such as Gel 1 and Gel 2, the later groups appear lower in the panel. Every color group is stored in a Scene, and comes back with it as long as the fixture is still in the same mode.

Coloring along the pixels — PIXELS

With PIXELS open on Home, the COLOR panel of a pixel fixture starts with a PIXELS section. It lays color out along the pixels in one go, on every fixture you have selected. It appears only where the pixels carry color that Kanau can write.

ButtonWhat it lays out
SOLIDEvery pixel follows the fixture's own color, as before
GRADIENTSTART on the first pixel, END on the last, blended in between
ALTERNATECOLOR 1 and COLOR 2 taking turns, or three colors with COLOR 3
RAINBOWThe hue circle along the pixels

The button you pressed lights amber, and so does the end or color you are setting — START, END, or COLOR 1 to COLOR 3. The sliders, presets and gels below then write to that one. There is nothing to confirm: the light changes as you go, and HISTORY steps back.

  • GRADIENT: Spread narrows or widens the blend. The blend runs through color temperature too, so START can be a warm white and END a color, on pixels that have those channels
  • ALTERNATE: Colors sets two or three, and Pixels per Color how many pixels each one takes
  • RAINBOW: Start Hue is the hue of the first pixel, and Span how far round the circle it goes along the fixture — 100% is once round. The 100%, 200%, 300% and 400% buttons under Span set it directly, and 100% puts it back to the default. Only Intensity is left below, because the rainbow decides the color

REVERSE swaps the ends, the colors or the direction. MIRROR makes the pattern symmetrical, with the same color at both ends; it does not work with ALTERNATE. SHIFT − and SHIFT + move the pattern one pixel, and the pixel pushed off one end comes back at the other. None of these appear on SOLID.

The row of dots is the first selected fixture's pixels, or every fixture's under ACROSS, read from what is going out. Tap a dot to set that pixel alone with the controls below, and tap it again or ALL to go back. Setting START or END again redraws the blend, pixels set by hand included.

With several fixtures, each takes the same pattern from its own first pixel — that is EACH. ACROSS joins them into one line in their order on Home, from the first pixel of the first fixture to the last pixel of the last. The pattern follows the pixel numbers, so a fixture with inverted pixels (chapter 06) starts from the same side on stage; its own dots show START on the right.

＋ saves the pattern and its colors as a palette and asks for a name. Tap a palette to apply it, and hold it to rename or delete it. Palettes are kept per model on this device, and one made on 16 pixels fits a fixture with 4. The shift and ACROSS are not part of it. With different models selected, the palette row is not there.

Fixtures with Lock on and fixtures running a color effect are left as they are. A Scene stores the colors like any other.

FIXTURES — one fixture as one step

Select two or more fixtures of the same model in the same mode, with PIXELS closed, and the same section appears under FIXTURES. Each fixture is one step, in their order on Home, and there is no EACH or ACROSS. SOLID gives them all the first fixture's color. Setting a fixture's color here clears its own pixel colors, so the fixture's color shows. Palettes are shared with the pixel section of the same model.

While a color effect is running

A color effect — RAINBOW, the colored fires, lightning and fluorescents — runs on any fixture that can make color, whatever mode it is in: RGB, CMY, Hue and Saturation, or xy.

While one runs, the color controls for that fixture are there to read, not to touch. A band at the top of the panel carries a dot lit in the color going out and the name of the effect, and says the color cannot be edited. Intensity still works. The values under the band are the color that comes back when the effect stops, so they stay where you left them.

A mode with no color, or an effect that does not move color, leaves the color controls working as usual.

The band also carries the values going out at this moment. Hold the round fixture icon to open this panel and read them.

06 Per-fixture settings

Limits, Lock and the raw channels of a single fixture.

Scroll down in the panel you get from holding a fixture icon, from COLOR, or from holding a model or group button.

Limits, Lock, Switch Function and BATTERY SAVE can be set for several fixtures at once. Mixed values show as — or n of m, and changing one applies it to all of them. Switch, Channels, Mode, Channel Roles and Patch appear only with a single fixture open.

Name and display

The title at the top of the panel is the fixture number and the name shown under the faders. Tap it to type a new name. The name belongs to the model, so every fixture of that model changes with it; clear it and the model's name comes back. The fixture's own name, number and model do not change. ‹ and › move to the next fixture. Label Color is the background of the number. No label color clears it.

Limits

Lower Limit and Upper Limit set the range you can work in. Change them with ±1 and ±5, or clear them. Outside a limit, Home shows orange hatching.

A cell's limits apply inside the body's. If the body is capped at 50, a cell capped at 80 still cannot pass 50.

Lock

WARNING

Fixture Lock holds a fixture's output where it is. The grand master, blackout, BATTERY SAVE, MIDI and the session do not change it — a locked fixture will not go out when you press blackout. A Scene recall is the one thing that can, and only in the case below. Check your locks before a take.

With Lock on, the fixture's output is held. Faders, piano mode, ⏻, color, raw channels, GM, B.O., BATTERY SAVE, MIDI and the session all leave it alone, and so do Scene recalls apart from the one case below.

Lock holds the DMX values at the fixture's addresses just before they go out; unlocking returns them to the current values. If a locked fixture's address or mode changes, or it is deleted, the old addresses keep sending the held values, and a red note in the Patch section says so. A lock left without its fixture appears in DMX Monitor, where UNLOCK releases it. Locks are saved in the show. An effect on a locked fixture stops where it was when you locked it.

There is one exception, and it is worth knowing before a take. A Scene that was stored while something was locked carries those locks with it. Recall such a Scene and its locks replace yours: a fixture you locked by hand is unlocked and takes the Scene's values, unless that Scene had it locked too. A Scene stored with nothing locked cannot do this — your locks hold, and the fixture does not move. Chapter 08 covers what a Scene stores.

With several fixtures selected and some of them locked, tapping clears every lock. With none locked, tapping locks them all.

Locking during a piano, FLASH or HIT press puts the temporary value back first, then holds. Changing limits while locked does not move the current value; it is brought into the new range when you unlock.

The other settings

ItemWhat it is
Switch FunctionWhat ⏻ does: NONE, ON/OFF, FLASH ON or FLASH OFF. ON/OFF is the default
BATTERY SAVEMarks this fixture for BATTERY SAVE. While BATTERY SAVE is on, Release for Now at the top of the panel brings a marked fixture back to its fader level until BATTERY SAVE is turned off, with the amount cut shown beside it
InvertPan and Tilt reverse the direction of Move effects on this fixture only. PIXELS reverses the order of this fixture's pixels, and its pixel faders on Home mirror with it
SwitchTurns this fader into an ON / OFF switch (chapter 04). Not the same as Switch Function, which sets what ⏻ does
ModeShows the current DMX mode. Change beside it opens Re-patch at the mode list
Channel RolesCorrects the role and name of each channel. Addresses do not move

Use Channel Roles when a patched fixture has channels being treated as the wrong function. To carry the fix into fixtures you patch later, edit the definition under Custom Fixtures instead.

Channels — the raw DMX (Advanced)

Use the dedicated controls for color, position and the rest first. Channels is for reaching functions those controls do not cover, one DMX channel at a time.

Channels lists everything in DMX order, under Dimmer, Color, Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus, Shapers and Control. Empty groups are hidden.

Kind of rowHow to work it
A continuous valueSlider, typing, or − and +
Named values and rangesA menu up to 12 entries, a searchable list beyond that
Commands like Reset or Lamp OffHold for the stated time. Let go early to cancel. Commands with no time are a tap
A grey row marked FADER or COLORDriven by a dedicated control, so it cannot be edited here
A row that depends on another channelShows what is available in the current state. When the row is not in use, a note names the channel and the range that switch it off

On a fixture whose second light source has its own dimmer, such as the Aura ring of a MAC Aura XIP, that dimmer is a row of its own here. The fader does not move it, but B.O., GM and BATTERY SAVE still act on it.

DMX at the top right switches between raw values and percentages. Home on a row returns it to its default; on Pan and Tilt that needs a hold. It is unavailable when nothing has been changed.

Changes to raw channels are recorded in HISTORY. Whether they also go into the current Scene follows chapter 08: AUTO UPDATE writes them as you work, MANUAL UPDATE waits for UPDATE, and a Scene with Lock This Scene on records nothing. On a pixel fixture, the body panel carries the body channels and a cell panel carries that cell's.

Changing the patch or the mode

Edit from Re-patch in the Patch section. You can see and change the universe and address, fixture number, model and mode. Next Free moves it to the next gap. Each change here is one step in HISTORY.

Change Mode shows the range before and after and any fixtures it would overlap, before you confirm. You can apply it to every fixture of that model; fixtures already in that mode are left as they are. Fixtures after it do not move on their own. When the new mode would overlap or run past channel 512, Change & Move to Next Free also appears, with Move to showing where it goes. Kanau changes only its own patch: set each fixture's own DMX address to its Move to value.

Delete This Fixture removes it after a confirmation, along with its values and settings, and takes it out of every Scene. HISTORY can undo it.

07 Position and beam

Pan, tilt, zoom, iris, frost and gobo on moving lights.

Pan and Tilt

Hold a fixture's round icon to open its panel, then switch to MOVE at the top. The switch is there whenever the selection holds a fixture with head or optics rows, and the side you left it on is the side that opens next time. A fixture with only strobe or effect channels has no MOVE; its rows stay under Channels (chapter 06), and it opens on COLOR. MOVE works on everything you have selected: the rows are grouped by model and mode, a value the whole group shares is shown, and where they differ it reads —.

% and DMX at the top of the MOVE face, beside the name of what you have open, switch between the fixture's own units and the raw DMX number. It is the same switch as the one under Channels and in the DMX monitor, so the whole console follows it. On DMX a field reads 0–255, or 0–65535 where the row is 16-bit.

Pan and Tilt read in degrees where the fixture data carries angles, and in percent where it does not. On a 16-bit fixture, coarse and fine sit on one row.

  • Drag near the handle and it moves by the distance your finger travels. Anywhere else scrolls the panel.
  • Type an angle into the field. Values outside the fixture's range are refused.
  • Step with ±0.1°, ±1°, ±10° and so on. The steps come from the unit and the resolution.
  • FINE and FINE+ slow it to 1/10 and 1/100.
  • Hold Home to send it to the fixture's own start position. Let go early to cancel.

With more than one fixture selected and their values apart, the slider and the step keys move them all by the same amount. The gaps between them are kept, and the ones that reach an end stop there while the rest carry on. Typing a value, Home, and picking from a list still put every fixture on the same value.

FAN sits on the Pan and Tilt rows whenever more than one fixture is selected. Turn it on and the slider becomes how far open they are: the middle stays where it is and the two ends open out by the same amount, reading ±n°. Turn it off and the slider goes back to moving them together.

Invert reverses the direction of Move effects on this fixture only; the slider and the angle it shows are not reversed. Nothing moves while the fixture is locked.

Dead ranges, where the DMX value does nothing, are skipped by both the slider and the steps. On a fixture whose default sits inside a dead range, the steps will not move: use the slider or type a value to get into the live range first.

Position is recorded in HISTORY. Whether it also goes into the current Scene follows chapter 08: AUTO UPDATE writes it as you work, MANUAL UPDATE waits for UPDATE, and a Scene with Lock This Scene on records nothing.

IMPORTANT

A Scene fade moves Pan, Tilt and the optics. They travel over the fade time the same way intensity does. What still switches the moment you recall is the values you choose rather than dial — gobo, prism, an animation wheel — and anything set in seconds or hertz. Chapter 08 has the list.

Zoom, iris, frost, focus and gobo

MOVE carries Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus and Shapers. A continuous value has a slider with the word for each end under it, step keys, and a field to type into. A named choice — a gobo, a prism, an animation wheel — sits between two arrow keys that walk the list one at a time, and a long list carries a magnifier to search. Home beside a row sends that one channel to the fixture's own start position. Anything outside these shelves is still under Channels (chapter 06).

To animate any of it, use Move and Beam in the EFFECT panel. Move works around wherever the head is pointing now, and layers on top of intensity effects.

Named looks

Each shelf — Position, Gobo, Beam, Focus and Shapers — carries its own row of named looks under its heading, with SAVE at the end of the row. A look holds its own value for each fixture, not one value shared by all of them.

  1. Select the fixtures and set them the way you want them.
  2. Tap SAVE. A Name box opens with a name already in it, such as POSITION 1.
  3. Tap SAVE again, or change the name first.

SAVE is only there while the selection holds a fixture with rows on that shelf.

Tapping a name puts the stored values back. It goes to the fixtures you have selected that are in that look; with nothing selected it goes to every fixture in it. A fixture that is not in the look is left alone, and so is one now in a different DMX mode from the one it was saved in.

Hold a name for Rename, Update — which writes what is set now into it — and Delete.

The looks belong to the show, not to a Scene. Tapping one puts the values there at once; store them in a Scene if you want them to travel over a fade time.

08 Storing and recalling looks — Scenes

A Scene is a stored look. Open Scenes, tap SAVE to store, tap a row to bring it back.

Storing a Scene

  1. Set intensity, color and any effects on Home.
  2. Tap Scenes → SAVE. It is stored straight away and becomes the current Scene.
  3. To rename it, tap Settings on that Scene's row and type a name.
  4. To protect what is in it, turn on Lock This Scene in the same panel.

The Settings here is the one inside the Scene's row. It is not the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

When your changes are recorded

Two buttons at the top of Scenes decide this, and a line under them says what the one you picked does. Until a Scene has been recalled or stored with SAVE, nothing is recorded, and the line says so; the same when the recalled Scene is locked. The choice is kept in the show file rather than on the phone, so a finished show opens the way you left it.

ButtonWhat happens once you have recalled a Scene
AUTO UPDATEEverything you then do to the light is recorded into that Scene as you lift your finger. There is nothing to press
MANUAL UPDATENothing is recorded until you tap UPDATE. Recalling another Scene throws away what you have not recorded, and does not ask

Switching between the two records nothing by itself. Going from MANUAL UPDATE to AUTO UPDATE does not write what is already waiting; AUTO UPDATE starts from your next move.

Under the current Scene's row, a strip says which of these is happening. The strip stays in the same position, and its label and appearance show whether UPDATE can be pressed.

StripWhenTap
LOCKED, greenThe Scene is locked, under either buttonNo
● RECORDING, the dot red and breathingAUTO UPDATE, not lockedNo. It is saying that what you do now is going in
UPDATE, dimMANUAL UPDATE, nothing differs from the recallNo
UPDATE, bright and blinkingMANUAL UPDATE, something differsYes. Records the current state

Under MANUAL UPDATE the difference is measured against the moment of the recall, or of storing it with SAVE. Take a fader to 30 and back to 50 and there is nothing left to record. While a fade is running nothing is counted, because those values are being moved by the machine and not by you. A FLASH, piano key or HIT you are holding is not recorded; SAVE, UPDATE and AUTO UPDATE take the look with your finger off.

What a Scene has recorded is not part of HISTORY.

Recalling and tidying

A recall brings back GM and B.O. as well, so it can raise the grand master or clear a blackout.

There is no way to read what a Scene has stored before you recall it. Its Settings hold the name, the fade time, the lock and Delete, and nothing else. Watching the GM figure at the top of the screen tells you what the value is now, not what the Scene will put there.

Stepping back repairs a recall; it does not stand in for checking first. The recall counts as one step in HISTORY, and stepping back restores GM and B.O. with everything else — only locks are never undone (chapter 10) — but by then the light has already moved, on stage as well as on screen.

What does keep a fixture out of a recall is Fixture Lock, unless that Scene was itself stored with locks (chapter 10); how fast the change is seen depends on what it is — the Fade section below says which values travel over the fade time and which switch at once.

Action or markWhat it does
Tap a rowRecalls when you lift your finger
NEXT / BACKThe next or previous Scene. It wraps around. Unavailable with only one Scene
● and an amber backgroundThe current Scene
▸The Scene NEXT will bring up
🔒 and a green edgeLocked against recording
SettingsName, fade time, lock, delete
SelectReorder, and select rows for Copy or Delete. It turns into Done
CopyCopies each selected Scene directly below itself
DeleteAsks first. Copy does not, because nothing is lost

The numbers are display order. The time under the name is when its contents last changed.

A copy takes the next free number as its name, keeps the contents and the fade time, and is never locked, even when the one it came from is. The copies become the selected rows, so pressing Copy again copies the copies.

BLIND — working without touching the lights

BLIND, the wide button under the title of Scenes, starts a copy of the console that sends nothing. A line under it says what it does; while BLIND is on, the button is amber with a light running along it. It starts from the faders, colors and effects as they are, or from where a running fade is heading. The lights keep doing what they were doing.

While BLIND is on, faders, color, effects and Scene recalls change the copy only; GM and B.O. still act on the lights. The band at the top, the edge of the screen and each panel are marked in amber. SAVE stores the BLIND look as a new Scene and UPDATE writes it into the current one; AUTO UPDATE and MANUAL UPDATE are grey, and BLIND always records the way MANUAL UPDATE does. Patch, Output, Session, Shows, HISTORY and Scene settings are closed, and in a fixture's panel the name cannot be typed and Label Color, BATTERY SAVE, Invert and Switch are hidden. Nothing you do in BLIND goes into HISTORY.

To leave, tap BLIND again, or BLIND at the top left of the screen. With unsaved changes it asks Update, Save New, Discard or Cancel. Leaving never changes the lights. A guest in a session has no BLIND.

Scene Lock

Turn on Lock This Scene for Scenes you want left alone. You can still recall them and still work the light, but nothing is recorded. LOCKED is shown on every locked row, not only on the current one.

Lock is stronger than either update button. A locked Scene never says RECORDING.

This is not the same as Fixture Lock. Scene Lock protects what is stored; Fixture Lock holds the output.

What is stored, and what is not

A Scene stores the intensities and colors, and with them settings such as GM and B.O. The table below says exactly what.

Stored and brought backNot stored
Intensity, CCT, G/M, crossfade, RGB, emitters, the name of the gel picked from a tableBATTERY SAVE
Raw channels such as position and gobo, cell color and intensity, effectsSwitch Function
Color groups, limits, Fixture Lock, ⏻ state, GM and B.O.—

A fixture you have locked is not changed by a recall, as long as the Scene was stored with nothing locked. If the Scene was stored while anything was locked, it carries those locks, and they replace yours on recall: a fixture you locked by hand is unlocked and takes the Scene's values, unless the Scene had it locked too.

Fade

Set it per Scene in Settings → Fade. 3 seconds is the default. There are presets of SNAP, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10, and ±0.1 and ±1 to adjust.

Intensity, color, cell values, color groups and GM travel over the fade time, and so do Pan, Tilt and the continuous beam values such as Zoom, Focus and Iris. That includes Amber, White, Lime, the fixture's own Hue and Saturation, x and y, and CMY; hue goes the short way round the circle. The faders move with them. A fixture you touch part-way — with a fader, a piano key, FLASH, ⏻, color or a MIDI knob, or from the guest in a session — leaves the fade and stays where you put it. A piano key or FLASH gives its value while held; let go and the fixture returns to where it was before you pressed, still out of the fade.

B.O., ⏻, limits, locks, effects, a fader set as a switch and the name of the gel do not interpolate, and neither do the raw values that are chosen rather than dialled: gobo, prism, an animation wheel, and anything set in seconds or hertz. They switch to the stored value the moment you recall, whatever the fade time says. Limits and locks are applied once, at the recall, so a limit or lock you change during the fade stays as you set it. Where you are coming from holds no position at all — an older Scene, for example — the head lands on the new value at once.

A Scene with effects in it restarts those effects on recall. Recalling a Scene with no effects releases whatever is running.

The recall itself is recorded in HISTORY as one step. Scenes are part of the show file.

09 Effects

Blink, fire, lightning and the rest, applied to your fixtures.

EFFECT on Home applies an effect to what you have selected. You can also tap the effect first and pick its fixtures next. The Effects tab at the bottom opens the same panel with EFFECT, and it is where everything that is running is managed.

Applying one

  1. On Home, tap the round icon of a fixture or a cell to select it.
  2. Open EFFECT.
  3. Tap an effect name. It starts immediately.

With nothing selected the names are still live. Tap one and a panel opens under that name to pick its fixtures; Done starts it. Cancel, or pulling the panel down, starts nothing.

The fader still sets intensity. While an effect runs, the EFFECT button carries its name, and the fixture icon and fader move with it. On a fader set as a switch, intensity effects do nothing; color effects still change its color.

At the top of the panel, a round icon stands for each step: the color of the light source in it, its number in the order underneath (not the fixture number), and the movement it is actually making. A step with nothing in it is a faint ring carrying +, and it stays dark as the chase goes past. The band above them shows the shape over time — in the effect's own color when it carries one, and plain when it does not.

Under the icons sit three keys: TOGETHER, SPREAD and STEPS. TOGETHER moves every light source as one; SPREAD gives each its own place in the run. Whichever is lit is the state, and with nothing selected both go dim and refuse. STEPS lights as well once you have set the seats by hand. The movement and the seats are two different things, so two keys can be lit at once and SPREAD over three steps reads as both. On the seats the app deals out itself, STEPS stays dark. RUNNER, FADE RUN and COMET always run apart.

STEPS opens the room where the steps live. Each step is a row with what is in it — Empty when there is nothing — and a SELECT of its own; + ADD STEP puts one on the end; EDIT brings out the handles, and a row dragged by its handle moves to another place in the order. Swipe a row to the left for DELETE. One step is the fewest there can be — and one step is TOGETHER.

Tapping an empty step opens the fixture list — the same one the step list's SELECT opens, with whatever is already in that step ticked. Tick to put a fixture in, untick to take it out. Done writes it; Cancel, or pulling the panel down, leaves the step as it was.

Tap the icons to pick out fixtures; the row under them says how many are MARKED, with ALL to mark every one and CLEAR to let them go. An icon marked … opens that fixture's own color and intensity panel on a hold — the same panel as the round icon on Home. Hold with several picked out and they open together.

Pause, release, restart

ActionWhat it does
BACKGoes back one step. With TOGETHER it goes back a whole cycle
NEXTGoes on one step, the same way
PAUSEFreezes the movement at the current intensity and position
RESUMECarries on from where it froze
RELEASEStops it and hands control back to the normal values. The settings stay in the list
STARTRuns a released effect again from the beginning
CLEARRemoves it from the list. It asks first

BACK and NEXT are the two arrow keys at the left of the row. They move while the effect is paused as well, so you can walk through it a step at a time. While something runs, the key at the right of the row says RELEASE; once it is stopped the same key says START, so the effect can be set going again without leaving the panel.

Adjust

ItemWhat it is
SpeedIn hertz. Decimals allowed
DepthHow far down it pulls the intensity. 100 reaches zero; 35 barely moves
SizeOn the kinds that move the head, in place of Depth: how far it swings, in degrees per axis. ±25.2° / ±12.6° swings both ways, 0–45° goes one way, and a single moving axis is named, as in Pan 0–90°. The biggest shapes reach ±90°. FINE beside it works like FINE on Home
How Often / CycleHow often it happens. Only on the kinds that use it
RoughnessHow ragged the flame is
WidthHow much of the rig is lit at once, for example 50% 2 / 4. On one fixture, or with TOGETHER, how long each beat stays lit; above 50%, PULSE and FADE RUN hold flat at the top
TailThe length of COMET's tail
RandomHow much the beat and the height wander. 0 keeps it regular
DramaOn the two fires. 0 is the real thing; higher makes it a stage fire

Which items appear depends on the effect. SIGNAL has a panel of its own instead.

Arrange

Arrange opens with how the effect treats color; the arrangement sits under it. The kinds that only move the head or the beam carry no color row.

ColorWhat it does
AUTOThe effect decides. The ones that carry no color of their own leave yours alone
COLORIt runs in the colors you set below. A color appears even on the kinds that have none
KEEPOnly the brightness moves. The color stays as you set it on the fader
ArrangementWhat it does
IN ORDEREvenly staggered by number
ALTERNATEOdd and even, half a cycle apart
WINGSMirrored out from the center
RANDOMIn a random order
BOUNCETurns around at each end
BUILDLights one at a time, then clears them all together
SPELLERLights one at a time, and once they are all on, everything flashes together three times
PASSLike IN ORDER, but fast through the middle and slow at the ends, the way a car goes past

Some kinds put a key in Arrange that only works while you hold it. CANDLE and BONFIRE carry FLARE and WIND — hold FLARE to make the fire flare up, WIND to let a gust beat it down. FLUO, FLUO FIZZ and FLUO DYING carry HIT: hold it and the tube fails, let go and it comes back. With CANDLE or BONFIRE on two or more fixtures, Arrange also carries ONE FIRE: the fixtures burn as one big flame, its rise and fall reaching each a little later along their order while each keeps its own flicker. It turns TOGETHER off. Under How often above, FLUO DYING fails on its own as well.

Runs under IN ORDER is how many patterns run at once, set with − n +. It will not go past the number of fixtures you have selected. Direction is FORWARD or REVERSE.

STEPS says how many steps the chase is running over, and how your fixtures or pixels are dealt into them: more fixtures than steps and a step holds several, more steps than fixtures and the spare ones stay dark. Press STEPS above to change how many there are, and which fixture sits in which.

INVERT swaps the lit and the dark. One step lighting up becomes one step going out, and a chase that fills becomes one that empties.

REPEAT on keeps the effect going round. Off, it runs once and holds its last look; press it again to run from the start.

The arrangement, Runs, STEPS and Direction only appear while SPREAD is on, and only on the kinds that run along the rig. INVERT and REPEAT sit outside that: REPEAT is always there, and INVERT on every kind but RAINBOW.

Both work with TOGETHER as well. Invert a blink set to 20% width and you get a short dip in an otherwise bright look; invert STROBE and you get short blackouts inside the light; turn REPEAT off and you get one flash that holds where it ends.

ADVANCED

Every effect carries an ADVANCED section below Arrange. It stays folded until you open it, and the folded heading says EDITED once you have changed something. RESET returns the settings inside ADVANCED to their starting values, and leaves everything above it alone.

BlockOnWhat you change
ColorsBeacons, PACHINKO, FIREWORKSEach lamp or flash, by name — RED, BLUE, AMBER and the rest
FROM / TOTOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARAThe two ends the street runs between. Set both the same and it holds one color
FAR / NEARLIGHTNINGThe far strike and the near one
TemperatureCANDLE, BONFIRELOW and HIGH in kelvin, in steps of 50
MAXFLUO, FLUO FIZZ, FLUO DYING, CANDLE, BONFIREHow hard the tube fails while HIT is held, or how strongly FLARE and WIND act. 10 to 100%, in steps of 10

This is where you change a fire's own color, because on AUTO it works that color out from its temperature.

Changing the target, and saving settings

Applies To → SELECT ▾ picks fixtures and groups. The selection is shared with Home, and the list stays open while you choose. A model opens into its fixtures, and a fixture with pixels opens again into ALL PIXELS and P1 … Pn. A fixture goes in whole or by pixel, not both.

With PIXELS open on Home, selecting a pixel fixture itself and applying an effect works as if you had selected all of its pixels: the arrangement, Runs and Direction play across the pixels, and the panel counts them — 16 selected for one fixture with 16 pixels. With PIXELS closed, each fixture is one step. An effect that is already running is adjusted where it lives, whichever way PIXELS is set.

SAVE beside Saved stores the settings you have dialled in, under a name. Saved cards are listed under SELECT ▾: pick one to apply it, and pick it again, ticked, to stop. To rename or delete one, open EDIT at the bottom of the list and pick it. Changes made there stay even if you close it by swiping down. An empty name is refused with Enter a name, and the old name stays. The fixtures are not part of a stored setting.

Select the fixtures already running along with the new ones, pick the same effect, and the speed, depth and phase carry over. Where the settings differ, it falls back to the defaults. To release just one fixture, select only that one and RELEASE.

Finding one by what you want

What you wantTry
Natural lightCANDLE, BONFIRE, LIGHTNING, WATER, WIND, TV
Light running along the rigRUNNER, FADE RUN, COMET
City lightNEON, SIGNAL, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, PACHINKO
BeaconsBEACON R/B, BEACON BLUE, BEACON RED, BEACON AMBER
Press camerasPAPARAZZI
Plain flashingBLINK, STROBE, PULSE, DOUBLE, JITTER, SPARKLE, RARE FLASH
Color on the moveRAINBOW
A failing fluorescentFLUO, FLUO FIZZ, FLUO DYING
Moving the headThe Move group
Moving zoom or goboThe Beam group
An old signMarquee

PAPARAZZI is camera flashes from a crowd. Each fixture fires on its own and stays dark in between, so the more you give it the less it looks like a pattern. How Often sets how many go off.

The two fires, and the failing tubes

CANDLE is a candle: in still air it sits almost still, and it only moves when something disturbs it. BONFIRE is a bonfire: a fast flicker around 2.7 Hz, with a gust of wind pushing it down now and then. Speed on BONFIRE goes up to 2.5 Hz.

Drama in Adjust sits on both and starts at 0, which is the real thing. Raise it and the fire becomes a stage fire: it stops going still, it reddens as it drops, and it flickers more than a real one would.

The fires take the color row in Arrange like any other effect. On AUTO they work their own color out from their temperature, and the temperature is under ADVANCED. Pick COLOR instead and they run in the color you set, keeping the flame's shape.

On AUTO, a fire whose fixtures carry both a color temperature channel and color of their own gets CCT and RGB to choose between. The two do not reach the same color. CCT rides the temperature channel, so the light makes the white it was calibrated for and the deepest embers stop at the lowest temperature it can reach. RGB rides the red, green and blue channels, and can paint the deep reds of the embers that a temperature channel cannot. Where a fixture has only one of the two, the choice does not appear.

FLUO is a tube that works. FLUO FIZZ is one that will not settle. FLUO DYING is one at the end of its life: the ends glow, it strikes and drops, and finally holds. On a fixture with pixels, only the two ends glow amber.

The full list

GroupEffects
BasicBLINK, STROBE, PULSE, DOUBLE, JITTER, SPARKLE, RARE FLASH, RUNNER, FADE RUN, COMET
LightsFLUO, FLUO FIZZ, FLUO DYING, CANDLE, BONFIRE, LIGHTNING, PAPARAZZI, TV, NEON, SIGNAL
PlacesBEACON R/B, BEACON BLUE, BEACON RED, BEACON AMBER, TOKYO, OSAKA, KYOTO, NARA, PACHINKO, WATER, FIREWORKS, LANTERNS, RAINBOW
MoveDRIFT, PASS, ORBIT, EIGHT, BOX, SPIRAL, SEARCH, BREATHE, HANDHELD, WIND, JUMP, BALLYHOO
BeamZOOM PULSE, ZOOM BREATHE, IRIS PULSE, FROST BREATHE, GOBO SHAKE

RUNNER, FADE RUN and COMET need several fixtures, or pixels. Move and Beam appear when the selected fixtures support them.

An amber dot at the top right of a name means the effect changes color as well. Without the dot, it uses the color you set by hand.

SIGNAL — traffic lights

SIGNAL is a crossing, and its name opens a panel of its own instead of applying anything. A crossing has two roads, and each road carries a light for the cars and one for the people crossing it: CAR · ROAD 1, WALK · ROAD 1, CAR · ROAD 2, WALK · ROAD 2.

Each signal is a card. Inside it sits a round icon for the whole signal, marked ALL, and beside it the lamps in a housing of their own — G Y R for the cars, R G for the people, in the order that country hangs them. An empty circle carries +, and the number of fixtures in the signal is under the name.

To fill a signal, select the fixtures on Home, open SIGNAL and tap an empty circle; a panel opens with them already ticked, and Done puts them in. Tapping a circle with nothing in hand opens the same panel to choose from. The ALL circle takes a fixture that is the whole signal and changes color for every phase; a lamp circle takes fixtures that light only for that lamp. A fixture picked for more than one lamp has its pixels divided between them, and pixels you placed by hand stay where you put them. One light source lives in one place only.

The two lines at the top say where the crossing stands — ⏸ WAITING · CAR · ROAD 1 · GREEN, with what NEXT will reach underneath and a bar for the run to it. While it runs the first word is RUNNING; between two stops, CHANGING.

ButtonWhat it does
PLAYRuns from where it is. Without REPEAT it stops at the head of the cycle, where ROAD 1 goes
PAUSEHolds where it is, mid-phase if need be
BACKGoes to the previous change
NEXTGoes to the next change
REPEATKeeps the cycle running by itself

A change is any point where a signal with fixtures in it changes lamp, so a crossing with people lights stops at their green and at their flashing green as well.

Below the buttons sit the country and ADVANCED, with a second key beside it for the signal you are editing: how long each lamp holds, with − 40s +, the color of each lamp, and RESET. One cycle stays 90 seconds — what you add to one phase comes out of the longest one.

SIGNAL 1 ▾ at the top switches between crossings and + NEW adds one. Each crossing keeps its own clock, country and signals.

Opening SIGNAL with fixtures that are in no crossing yet takes you to an empty crossing, and makes a new one when none is empty. Fixtures already in a crossing open that crossing.

Back in the EFFECT panel, when every selected fixture is in a crossing, the top of the panel shows that crossing's two lines, and the row of buttons under it drives that crossing: BACK, NEXT, PLAY or PAUSE, and REPEAT. PAUSE lights amber while the crossing runs, and REPEAT while it is on. Applying an effect takes the fixtures out of the crossing, and the top goes back to the effect.

Marquee — the old bulb-sign shapes

Marquee is a row of cards in the panel, just under Basic. They are the shapes an old bulb sign ran, under the names the signs used; pressing one sets the shape and the arrangement together. From there you adjust it with the same knobs as every other effect.

A card does not decide how many steps there are. Pressing one gives you a step for each light source you have selected, and for the dark gaps of a real sign you add steps with + at the head of the icon row. The color arrives as COLOR, set to the warm glow of old tungsten; KEEP runs it in the color you made on the fader instead.

PatternWhat it does
CHASEOne bulb runs along the sign
DARK CHASEAll lit but one, and the dark one runs
CRAWLTwo side by side run together
BOUNCERuns to the end and comes back the way it came
BUILDLights one by one, then all clear together
FILLFills from the front, then empties from the front
FLIP FLOPOdd and even take turns
FLASHAll on, all off
TWINKLEEach bulb blinks on its own
SPELLERSpells out, then flashes three times

DARK CHASE is CHASE with INVERT on, and FILL is BUILD with INVERT on. The same switch turns any of the running shapes inside out.

Speed is in hertz, as everywhere else. Depth is how dark an unlit step goes: below 100 it keeps a little glow, like a filament cooling. Direction, BACK and NEXT work as they do on the rest.

Layering LIGHT, MOVE and BEAM

One fixture can carry a LIGHT effect for intensity and color, a MOVE effect for the head, and a BEAM effect at once. Choosing another effect in the same lane replaces it. Cells take LIGHT only. On a fixture whose second light source has its own dimmer, such as the Aura ring of a MAC Aura XIP, LIGHT moves the main light only.

Opening the panel shows the first running lane, in the order LIGHT, MOVE, BEAM.

Managing them from the Effects tab

EDIT opens an effect's settings. RELEASE / START, PAUSE / RESUME and CLEAR are there. A released effect stays in the list, marked RELEASED, and CLEAR still removes it. EDIT, CLEAR and the row's chips act on that row's own lane — the head or the intensity — so a blink and a figure-eight on one fixture stay apart.

n ∨ opens the fixture chips for that row; n ∧ folds them again. The × on a chip drops that one fixture. The + adds what you have selected, a group, a model, or All. RELEASE ALL and START ALL apply to everything. Each crossing has a row of its own — SIGNAL 1, SIGNAL 2 and so on — with EDIT and CLEAR.

Effects keep counting through a blackout. Unlocked fixtures go dark and pick the movement up where it is when you clear it. On a locked fixture the effect stops where it was when you locked it; unlock it and it picks up where the effect has got to. Fixture Lock is covered in chapter 10.
